analysis: All changes are test-only. FlintResponseFormatTests.swift (line 361) adds a `.toolCallDelta` case to the event switch so it stays exhaustive; a completed delta counts as a call. The `toolsWithAFormatNeverReturnCalls` test still asserts that calls==0 for frames, so the no-call-under-response_format property is still checked. NemotronSuperLocalOutputTests.swift (lines 37-39) adds a `.toolCallDelta` case that fails the test if the Super output ever streams fragments. This pins the hold-until-validation behavior and does not weaken it. ProviderLoopStreamChunkTests.swift (lines 59, 282-283, 299, 312) adapts the tests to the new OpenAIToolCallDelta type, where `function` is optional, and to the hash encoding of tool-call deltas. The tests keep the determinism check on encodeToolCallsForHash. Test code has no production attack surface, and I found no change to the ADV-001 or T-008 boundaries in it. The production sources were not supplied. Integration should check the following: (1) that streaming toolCallDelta emission, which this test fixture implies, runs only after the same validation (declared names, schema, tool_choice, parallel limits) as the held-call path, and that this holds for Flint and Super; (2) that encodeToolCallsForHash, which now takes optional-field deltas, stays collision-resistant for the response-hash and attestation paths; (3) that fragments are encrypted under the same fail-closed paths as other chunks (T-008). These cannot be judged from the supplied test-only diffs, so deeper review of the production changes is warranted.
